_comment: Feed audit 2026-08-17. lean labels are PRIORS for calibration testing only - never passed to the scorer.
_calibration_note: News Service of Florida is the wire anchor. Its copy should score near-neutral. NSF is subscription-only; pull its text from republishers with attribution.

sources.name: Florida Politics
sources.notes: Explicitly crawl-permitted: robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' (empty = allow all) plus a Yoast sitemap_index.xml. The earlier 'blocks bots' finding was our own fault - the site 403s any UA advertising an outdated browser ('Update Browser Required'), and we were sending Chrome/127. An honest named crawler gets 200. Feed carries full text and named bylines. HIGH VELOCITY: ~10 items per 4 hours into a 10-item window, so page 1 alone loses most output between twice-daily runs - hence catchup_pages.

sources.name: News Service of Florida
sources.notes: Subscription wire; text pulled from a republisher's author archive, which carries content:encoded in full and paginates (?paged=N) for backfill. Direct feed https://newsserviceflorida.com/search/?q=&t=article&f=rss is headlines-only - keep it for the re-headline check: if a republisher retitles the wire, this source is scoring the republisher's edit, not NSF. Body text opens with 'By The News Service of Florida' - the blinding step MUST strip it or the near-zero calibration is circular. One republisher is a thin anchor; find more (also unlocks the same-story-across-outlets editing signal). Second republisher confirmed: tampabay.com carries the wire as 'By News Service of Florida'. Two republishers make the same-story editing comparison possible - it needs a per-republisher source_id scheme (nsf@<outlet>) that is not built yet.

sources.name: News Service of Florida (direct wire, headlines only)
sources.notes: NSF's own headlines, direct from the wire. The control for calibration test #1: diff against the republished titles in 'nsf' to detect retitling, and against what 'nsf' does NOT carry to measure the republisher's selection - that is what validate_anchor.py reads. DO NOT RE-AUDIT: reactivated headlines_only on 2026-08-21 to grow the sample and immediately 429'd, from a residential IP and from an Actions runner (Azure eastus) alike. Both times every other source returned 200 in the same run, so it is this host, not our network and not our UA. The limiter is custom - text/plain body carrying client_ip and request_id, no Retry-After, no cf-ray - and it is recent: the same honest UA got 200 here on 2026-08-18 and the 15 stored headlines were pulled 08-13 to 08-17. Set 'blocked' rather than active because an errored active source alarms health.py on every run. The 15 headlines remain usable; the sample is frozen, not lost. Route to a bigger sample is the second republisher (tampabay.com) via the nsf@<outlet> scheme, which also gives body text this feed never had. Never score: headline-only.

sources.name: Tallahassee Reports
sources.notes: Apache, no edge blocking; robots.txt permissive with Crawl-delay 10. exclude_authors keeps the NSF republications out of this source_id - they belong to 'nsf', and both feeds reach the same URL. Of 10 sampled entries only 1 original was state-Capitol (the rest local: city commission, schools, real estate, HS sports) so a relevance filter is needed before scoring. prior_lean deliberately null - needs an editorial call on its ORIGINAL reporting, not on the wire copy it reprints.

sources.name: Capitol News Service
sources.notes: Defunct. Owner retired in 2022; the site lingered and served stale items until Apr 2025. Do not scrape - there is nothing being published. Removed from the target outlet count.

sources.name: WFSU News
sources.notes: Measured Aug 17, not worth the workaround. index.rss returns 0 entries. The tags/tallahassee-politics.rss feed exists but is dormant - 10 entries spanning Oct 2022 to Jan 2026, summary-only at ~179 chars. news-sitemap-content.xml is fresh but 31 of 36 items are /npr-news/ national wire and exactly 1 is local. Deprioritised: there is barely any local Capitol journalism here to measure.

sources.name: Tampa Bay Times
sources.notes: NOT headlines-only - that was wrong. The Arc feed carries full article text (sampled 1031/836/545/399 words) with named bylines. Verified 2026-08-18, re-verified 2026-08-19 (76 entries, bodies of 7445/1716/709/157/1041/270 words at feed positions 0/1/2/20/40/60). Requires the Accept header: without it the endpoint returns 0 entries. ALSO AN NSF REPUBLISHER, labelled 'By News Service of Florida' - excluded here so it does not dilute the Times' own score. Harvesting NSF from here needs main-feed filtering (Arc has no author archive), unlike the Tallahassee Reports route. THE ARTICLE PAGES ARE WALLED AND ALWAYS WERE - status ready is still correct because we never fetch them. Every article URL returns 200 and extracts to the same 75-word subscriber-comments block ('Anyone can view a sampling of recent comments, but you must be a Times subscriber to contribute'), byte-identical across articles and publication dates: the body ships in the HTML but only inside JSON-LD, which declares isAccessibleForFree False and hides the rendered copy behind a .paywall selector. Investigated 2026-08-19 as a suspected metered paywall exhausted by our own probing. It is not metered - a cookieless first request is walled, the wall does not vary by article or date, and the feed returned full text from the same IP in the same minute. Nothing resets and there is nothing to wait for. fulltext_from is 'feed' precisely because of this: do NOT repoint extraction at the article URL, and do not downgrade this source on article-page evidence.

sources.name: Miami Herald
sources.notes: DO NOT CRAWL. robots.txt carries a written prohibition (read 2026-08-18): automated scraping and specifically 'text and data mining activities' require prior written permission. Its User-agent:* stanza only blocks template paths, so article paths are technically allowed - the prohibition is in prose referencing their ToS. Also blocks anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / GPTBot / CCBot / Scrapy on /*.html, and blocks archive.org_bot + ia_archiver, so there is no Wayback route either. Separately it never answers us: 45s read timeout even on robots.txt. Only route is written permission. Coverage EXISTENCE is still trackable via sayfie (linked x25 on one homepage), which is all the omission analysis needs. Log in the exception log.

sources.name: Orlando Sentinel
sources.notes: DO NOT CRAWL. robots.txt (read 2026-08-18) carries a written Tribune Publishing prohibition covering: text and data mining as an EU DSM Art. 4 rights reservation; use for 'retrieval augmented generation, grounding, training, or development of machine learning models'; caching or archiving; and any commercial purpose. Its User-agent:* stanza only blocks wp-admin paths, so article paths are technically crawlable - the prohibition is in prose referencing tribpub.com terms. Blocks anthropic-ai / ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / Claude-User / GPTBot / CCBot, and Archive.org_bot + ia_archiver, so no Wayback route. Separately 403s an honest crawler on /feed/ and the Arc path. Notably allow-lists commercial partners (AmazonAdBot, grapeshot, Twitterbot, EchoboxBot, mrfCompass) while excluding independent analysis - a documentable gatekeeping asymmetry. sun-sentinel.com is the same Tribune stable and presumably identical terms; Sayfie links it x13, so existence stays trackable there too.

sources.name: Tallahassee Democrat
sources.notes: No RSS. Gannett's rssfeeds.tallahassee.com returns an HTML app shell, and /feed/ + the Arc path 404 (tested 2026-08-18). Existence trackable via sayfie, which links tallahassee.com x12.

sources.name: Sayfie Review
sources.notes: Link aggregator, NOT an outlet: 241 off-site vs 18 on-site links on one homepage. robots.txt leaves the blanket disallow commented out; only a Googlebot crawl-delay 3. No usable RSS (declared feed is javascript:void(0)) so ingestion means parsing the homepage. Value is coverage EXISTENCE for outlets we cannot crawl - one homepage carried floridapolitics.com x29, miamiherald x25, sun-sentinel x13, tallahassee.com x12, palmbeachpost x10. Feeds the omission feed and bill-vs-coverage matching, never a bias score. Human-curated: its own selection bias belongs in the priors disclosure. STATUS planned - the index scraper and its table are not built yet.
